title: Extending partial edge-colorings of bounded size in Cartesian products of graphs
summary: This paper studies edge-precoloring extensions in Cartesian products of graphs, motivated by a conjecture of Casselgren, Petros, and Fufa. We formulate a general hypothesis stating that if every edge-precoloring of $G$ and $H$ of sizes $k<χ'(G)$ and $l<χ'(H)$, respectively, is extendable, then any edge-precoloring of $G \square H$ of size $k+l+1$ can be extended to a proper $(χ'(G)+χ'(H))$-coloring. We provide partial progress toward this conjecture by establishing the result in cases where $k<Δ(G)$, $G$ is a triangle-free $r$-regular graph and $H$ is a star, an even cycle, a path or, more…
